reason.flow-missing: The challenge flow is gone: its entry client was removed or is not connected to anything.
reason.path-missing: There is no path from the client to the required block — finish wiring the chain.
reason.sync-instead-of-async: Slow work is called synchronously, so the user waits for it. Make the edge asynchronous and put a queue in front.
reason.above-target: The value is above the allowed threshold.
reason.below-target: The value is below the required threshold.
reason.node-saturated: A block is overloaded: utilization exceeds the limit. Add instances, shard it, or take reads off with a cache.
reason.over-budget: Cost exceeds the budget. Look at egress and storage first — that is usually where the money goes.
reason.not-enough-capacity: Provisioned space will not cover the retention horizon. Add capacity, compress the data, or shorten retention.
reason.store-missing: The write path never reaches durable storage — there is nowhere to keep the data.
reason.replication-too-low: Fewer copies than required: losing one node loses the write. Raise the replication factor.
reason.single-instance: A block on the critical path runs as a single instance — that is a single point of failure. Add a second replica.
reason.single-az: The critical path lives in one availability zone, so its failure takes everything down. Spread the blocks across at least two AZs.
reason.lag-too-high: Replica or queue lag exceeds the limit. Add consumers or partitions, or reduce the replicated volume.
reason.anomaly-present: Anomalies show up at the required consistency level. Read from the primary, or switch on CAS or transactions.
reason.anomaly-above-threshold: The anomaly rate is above the challenge threshold.
reason.not-enough-regions: Fewer regions than required. Add a region and place the critical path inside it, not an empty frame.
reason.residency-not-declared: Data residency is not declared. Set it in the multi-region policy, otherwise the requirement cannot be proven.
reason.client-too-far: The client is too far from the entry point: RTT eats the latency budget. Move the edge closer — a CDN or a regional entry.
reason.rpo-too-high: RPO exceeds the target: a region failure would lose too much data. Tighten replication or make critical writes synchronous.
reason.rto-too-high: RTO exceeds the target: switching regions takes too long. Lower the DNS TTL and keep the standby warm.
reason.control-auth-on-edge: No authentication at the perimeter. Verify the token at the entry instead of reinventing it in every service.
reason.control-no-direct-client-to-db: The client talks to storage directly. Drop the edge and put a service or a gateway in between.
reason.control-tls-terminate: There is nothing to terminate TLS on. Add a gateway or a CDN at the perimeter.
reason.control-rate-limit-at-edge: No rate limiting at the perimeter. Set a per-client request limit on the gateway.
reason.consistency-model-off: The consistency anomaly model is off — there is nothing to check the requirement against.
reason.no-load: There is no load: add a client and connect it to the scheme.
reason.no-growth: Data does not grow: no block writes anything to storage.
reason.no-async-edges: There are no asynchronous edges — nothing can lag.
reason.no-multi-region: There is no multi-region setup, so RPO and RTO have nothing to be measured against.

realism.param-out-of-range: Parameter “{{param}}” = {{value}} is outside the realistic range {{min}}…{{max}}. Fine in the sandbox, not at grading time.
realism.given-node-removed: The given block “{{node}}” was removed. It is part of the challenge statement and must stay on the scheme.
realism.given-param-changed: Parameter “{{param}}” of a given block was changed: {{actual}} instead of {{expected}}. The statement cannot be edited.
realism.too-many-nodes: {{nodes}} blocks against a limit of {{maxNodes}}. The challenge asks for a simpler solution — drop the extras.
realism.forbidden-type: Block “{{type}}” is forbidden by the challenge.
realism.group-not-allowed: Group “{{group}}” is not among the ones allowed for this challenge.
realism.empty-edge: Empty edge: fanout or call share is zero. No traffic flows through it, so the capability does not count.
realism.sampling-too-low: Log sampling {{samplingRate}} is below the minimum {{min}}. Observability cannot be switched off to save money.
realism.replica-lag-below-physics: Replica lag {{replicaLagMs}} ms is below the physical minimum {{minimumMs}} ms: data cannot travel faster than the link.
realism.empty-region: The region is empty: not a single block inside. An empty frame does not count as a standby.
realism.external-does-core-work: An external API does the core work of requirement {{requirement}}. That is not a solution — design that part yourself.
realism.consistency-model-required: The challenge requires the “{{required}}” model, but “{{actual}}” is enabled. Restore the consistency setting.

lint.async-for-slow-work: Slow operations sit behind a queue — the user does not wait for them.
lint.auth-at-edge: Authentication happens at the perimeter instead of being reinvented in every service.
lint.backpressure: Queues and concurrency are bounded: there is backpressure instead of an infinite buffer.
lint.cache-before-hot-db: A cache stands in front of the read-heavy store.
lint.cdn-for-static: Static content is served through a CDN rather than straight from the origin.
lint.circuit-breaker-external: External dependencies have a timeout and a circuit breaker.
lint.conflict-strategy-declared: The active-active setup declares an explicit conflict resolution strategy.
lint.dlq-present: Consumers have a DLQ and a retry cap.
lint.dns-ttl-matches-rto: The DNS TTL matches the target RTO — a region switch will make it in time.
lint.graceful-degradation: There is a degradation path: stale data from cache when a dependency fails.
lint.idempotency-on-at-least-once: At-least-once consumers carry an idempotency key.
lint.idempotent-writes: Retried writes are marked idempotent — a repeat will not create a duplicate.
lint.multi-az: The critical path spans at least two availability zones.
lint.multi-az-and-region: The scheme survives both an AZ failure and a region failure.
lint.observability-sampled: Traces and logs are sampled instead of being written one to one.
lint.partitioned-by-key: Sharding uses a meaningful key and there is no hot partition.
lint.rate-limit-at-edge: The perimeter enforces a request rate limit.
lint.read-replicas: The read-heavy SQL store has read replicas and reads actually go there.
lint.residency-respected: Data under a residency requirement never leaves its region.
lint.ryw-where-it-matters: Where a user reads their own write, the read does not land on a lagging replica.
lint.at-least-once-not-idempotent: At-least-once consumers without an idempotency key ({{consumers}}): a redelivery applies the effect twice. Add an idempotency key or deduplication.
lint.blob-in-sql: Files live in a relational database (row {{rowSizeBytes}} B against a {{thresholdBytes}} B threshold): caches and backups blow up. Keep blobs in object storage and only a reference in the database.
lint.cache-no-ttl-no-eviction: Caches without TTL and eviction policy: {{caches}}. Memory will run out while data silently goes stale — set a TTL and an eviction policy.
lint.chatty-fanout: A synchronous fanout of {{fanout}} calls against a threshold of {{threshold}}: the slowest tail will own your p99. Batch the reads or answer asynchronously.
lint.client-to-db-direct: The client talks to storage directly ({{edges}} edges): no authorization, no limits, no cache. Put a service or a gateway in between.
lint.cross-region-sync-write: Synchronous writes over a cross-region link ({{edges}} edges, RTT {{rttMs}} ms) add that RTT to the p99 of every write. Write locally and replicate asynchronously.
lint.deep-sync-chain: A synchronous chain {{depth}} hops deep against a threshold of {{threshold}}: latencies add up and failure probabilities multiply. Flatten the calls or move the tail to a queue.
lint.dns-ttl-vs-rto: DNS TTL {{ttlSec}} s exceeds the target RTO {{rtoTargetSec}} s — clients physically cannot move in time. Cut the TTL to a fraction of the RTO.
lint.hot-partition: Hot partition: a share of {{hotShare}} of the traffic lands on one key against a threshold of {{threshold}}. Salt the shard key or put the hot slice in a cache.
lint.log-everything: Logs cost more than compute ({{logsCostMonth}} against {{computeCostMonth}} $/mo) and are written unsampled. Turn on sampling and retention.
lint.n-plus-one: Fanout of {{fanout}} to the store per incoming request against a threshold of {{threshold}} — a textbook N+1. Fetch the batch in one query.
lint.no-timeout: Edges without a timeout: {{edges}}. A hung call holds a thread and drags neighbours down — set a timeout from the latency budget.
lint.orphan-node: Blocks without traffic: {{nodes}}. Connect them or remove them — they only add complexity and cost.
lint.over-provisioned: Every node is idle (peak {{maxUtilization}} against a threshold of {{threshold}}) — you are paying for air. Reduce the instance count.
lint.read-replica-for-ryw: Reads of a user's own write go to an asynchronous replica ({{stores}} stores). Pin the session to the primary or read your own writes from it.
lint.region-without-capacity: If region {{region}} fails, the rest cannot absorb it: {{needRps}} needed, {{spareRps}} rps spare. Keep N+1 headroom.
lint.residency-violation: Data under a residency requirement leaves its region ({{edges}} edges). Restrict replication or separate personal data from the rest.
lint.retry-without-budget: Retries without a breaker ({{edges}} edges, up to {{retries}} attempts): degradation turns into an avalanche. Add a retry budget and a circuit breaker.
lint.rf1-on-durable-data: Durable data kept in a single copy ({{stores}} stores): one disk failure and it is gone. Raise replication to at least three copies.
lint.rmw-without-cas: Read-modify-write on a contended key without CAS or locks ({{stores}} stores). Version the record or use a conditional update.
lint.silent-lww: Active-active with last-write-wins: losing writes are dropped silently. Choose a deliberate conflict resolution strategy or a CRDT.
lint.spof-on-critical-path: A single point of failure on the critical path ({{nodes}} blocks). Add a second replica and a second availability zone.
lint.sync-call-to-slow-op: A synchronous call to an operation taking {{responseSec}} s against a threshold of {{thresholdSec}} s. Answer the user immediately and hand the work to a queue.
lint.unbounded-queue: An unbounded buffer ({{nodes}} blocks): the queue grows until memory runs out. Set a depth limit and an alert on lag.
lint.write-through-no-persistence: A cache acts as the source of truth without persistence ({{caches}} caches). A restart wipes the data — write to durable storage.

findings.overloaded: Overloaded: {{nodeNames}} runs at {{utilizationPct}}% and is bound by {{boundBy}} at a capacity of {{capacity}} req/s; {{dropped}} req/s are dropped. Add instances, shard it, or cut the traffic.
findings.saturated: Close to the limit: {{nodeNames}} runs at {{utilizationPct}}%, bound by {{boundBy}} at a capacity of {{capacity}} req/s. The queue will grow at peak.
findings.retry-storm: Retry storm: the model did not converge — retries add load faster than the system drains it. Reduce the retry count, add backoff and a circuit breaker.
findings.retry-amplification: Retries inflate the load: {{nodeNames}} receives {{amplificationPct}}% more requests because of repeats. Raise the timeout or enable exponential backoff.
findings.spof: Single point of failure: {{nodeNames}} has no standby — losing it breaks the whole request path. Add a second replica or a second zone.
findings.hot-key: Hot key: {{nodeNames}} takes {{hotKeyRps}} req/s on a single shard whose capacity is {{perShardCapacity}} req/s. Spread the key out or put a local cache in front.
findings.client-direct-to-store: The client talks to the store directly ({{nodeNames}}). Put a service or a gateway in between — otherwise there is no authorization, no limits and no cache.
findings.retry-without-idempotency: Retries without idempotency: {{retries}} retries are configured, but the operation is not idempotent ({{nodeNames}}). A retry creates a duplicate — add an idempotency key.
findings.backlog-growing: The backlog grows: the producer emits {{producerRps}} msg/s while the consumer drains {{consumerCapacity}} msg/s — the lag adds {{growthPerSec}} msg/s. Add consumers or partitions.
findings.read-heavy-without-cache: Reads without a cache: {{nodeNames}} serves {{readRps}} reads/s at {{utilizationPct}}% utilization. A cache in front of the store removes most of that load.
findings.egress-dominates: Traffic dominates the bill: egress is {{sharePct}}% of the cost ({{egressCost}} $/mo). Enable a CDN, compress responses, or keep the traffic inside the region.
findings.unmodelled: No model: {{nodeNames}} is not simulated yet — its capacity and latency are excluded from the estimate.
findings.anomaly-stale-read: Stale reads: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}% of reads) return outdated data because of replica lag ({{nodeNames}}). Read from the primary where freshness matters.
findings.anomaly-read-your-writes: The user does not see their own write: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) hit a replica before the change lands ({{nodeNames}}). Pin the session to the primary.
findings.anomaly-lost-update: Lost updates: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}% of writes) overwrite each other ({{nodeNames}}). Use versions, CAS, or transactions instead of read-modify-write.
findings.anomaly-write-conflict: Write conflicts: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) edit the same key from different regions ({{nodeNames}}). Pin the key to one region or switch to CRDTs.
findings.anomaly-lost-write-lww: Writes are lost to last-write-wins: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) are silently discarded as losers ({{nodeNames}}). Change the conflict resolution strategy.
findings.anomaly-duplicate-processing: Duplicate processing: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) are handled twice ({{nodeNames}}). At-least-once without idempotency causes double effects.
findings.unknown-component: Unknown block "{{type}}": it is not in the catalog and is excluded from the estimate.
findings.dangling-edge: Dangling edge: one of its ends points at a block that does not exist.
findings.no-entry-point: No entry point: add a client — without one there is no load to simulate.
findings.cycle-detected: Cycle in the scheme: {{size}} blocks call each other in a loop — latency there is approximated.
findings.unreachable-node: Unreachable block: {{nodeNames}} receives no traffic from any client.
findings.deep-sync-chain: Deep synchronous chain: {{depth}} hops in a row starting at {{nodeNames}}. Every hop multiplies latency and failure odds — move part of it off the request path.
